biggest_catch: New customers only: anyone with signing authority on an existing Springs Valley consumer checking account — or who closed one within the past 90 days — is ineligible.
catches: Open a new Free eZChecking account between May 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026.

Within 60 days of opening, all four qualifying activities must be completed: (1) receive direct deposits totaling $1,500+; (2) open a new Focus Savings account and maintain an average daily balance of at least $100 for 60 days; (3) enroll in Online Banking; (4) enroll in eStatements.
A qualifying direct deposit is a recurring electronic deposit of a paycheck, pension, Social Security, or other regular monthly income made by an employer or outside agency.
Both accounts must remain open and in good standing to receive the bonus.
New personal checking customers only — not eligible if any signer has signing authority on an existing Springs Valley consumer checking account or closed one within the past 90 days.
Limit one bonus per customer per calendar year; not valid with any other offer; offer may be modified or discontinued at any time.
Minimum opening deposit: $50 for Free eZChecking; $100 for Focus Savings.
Bonus is credited to the eligible checking account no later than 90 days after all conditions are met, identified as '250 Bonus' on the statement.
The bonus may be reported on IRS Form 1099 and may be considered taxable income.

steps: Open a new Free eZChecking account ($50 minimum opening deposit) between May 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026.
Within 60 days of opening, set up and receive direct deposits totaling $1,500 or more (paycheck, pension, Social Security, or other regular monthly income from an employer or outside agency).
Within the same 60 days, open a new Focus Savings account ($100 minimum opening deposit) and maintain an average daily balance of at least $100 for 60 days.
Enroll in Online Banking and eStatements within 60 days of opening.
Keep both accounts open and in good standing; the $250 bonus is credited within 90 days after all conditions are met.
Expect the bonus to be reported on IRS Form 1099 and to be taxable income.
